edges.description: Neither allele yields an enzyme capable of catalysis, so hepatocytes have no urocanate hydratase activity.
With the second step absent, flux from histidine to glutamate cannot proceed past urocanate.
Urocanate produced upstream has no onward route and accumulates.
Circulating urocanate is filtered and appears in urine, where it is detected by organic-acid screening or untargeted metabolomics.

nodes.description: Two UROC1 alleles that cannot produce a functional enzyme. Reported alleles include missense changes that disrupt folding or abolish substrate binding and a recurrent nonsense allele; ClinGen's curation counts four unique missense variants and one nonsense variant across the reported human cases.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the urocanase gene UROC1 are associated with urocanic aciduria.
evidence.snippet: This report describes the first putative mutations, p.L70P and p.R450C, in the coding region of the UROC1 gene in a girl with urocanic aciduria presenting with mental retardation and intermittent ataxia.
Four unique missense variants and one nonsense varaint have been reported in humans thus far.

nodes.description: Excretion of urocanic acid in urine, the defining and obligate laboratory finding. Detected historically by urine paper chromatography on newborn screening specimens and now by untargeted metabolomic analysis of urine and plasma.

evidence.snippet: One family was asymptomatic except for the characteristic urocanic aciduria

nodes.description: The histidine degradation route is interrupted at its second step. Histidine ammonia-lyase upstream continues to deaminate histidine to urocanate, so the block is a substrate trap rather than a simple loss of product.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism for disease is biallelic loss of function, with loss of enzyme activity resulting in a buildup of the prior metabolite in the histidine metabolic pathway, urocanic acid.

evidence.reference_title: Untargeted metabolomics identifies unique though benign biochemical changes in patients with pathogenic variants in UROC1.
evidence.snippet: Notably, histidine levels were found to be within normal limits in all samples.

nodes.description: Absent or non-functional urocanase in the hepatocyte cytosol. The enzyme normally hydrates trans-urocanate to an imidazolone-propanoate intermediate, the second step of histidine degradation.

evidence.snippet: Urocanic aciduria is caused by a deficiency in the enzyme urocanase (E.C. 4.2.1.49) encoded by the gene UROC1.

nodes.description: Urocanate accumulates in hepatocytes and is released into the circulation and filtered into urine, producing the urocanic aciduria for which the disorder is named. This is the demonstrated and obligate consequence of the enzyme block.

evidence.reference_title: Untargeted metabolomics identifies unique though benign biochemical changes in patients with pathogenic variants in UROC1.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe two phenotypically normal siblings with compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in UROC1 and characteristic biochemical evidence of urocanase deficiency collected utilizing untargeted metabolomic analysis.
